title: An abelian degree-zero category from cohomology closure in a derived subcategory
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $D(\mathcal A)$ be its ordinary unbounded derived category with cohomology functors $H^q$ and single-complex functor $S(M)=M[0]$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal T$ be a strictly full triangulated subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], where strictly full means closed under all ambient isomorphisms. Assume that $S(H^q(K))$ belongs to $\mathcal T$ for every $K\in\mathcal T$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$. Let $\mathcal B$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ on objects $M$ with $S(M)\in\mathcal T$. The restriction $S:\mathcal B\to\mathcal T$ is fully faithful, and its essential image is exactly the objects $K\in\mathcal T$ with $H^q(K)=0$ for $q\ne0$. For a morphism $f:M\to N$ in $\mathcal B$ and any ambient cone triangle $S(M)\xrightarrow{S(f)}S(N)\to D\to S(M)[1]$, the ambient kernel and cokernel of $f$ are canonically isomorphic to $H^{-1}(D)$ and $H^0(D)$, respectively, and belong to $\mathcal B$. The subcategory $\mathcal B$ contains zero and finite biproducts, is abelian with the ambient kernels and cokernels, and is closed under ambient extensions: if $0\to M\to L\to N\to0$ is exact in $\mathcal A$ with $M,N\in\mathcal B$, then $L\in\mathcal B$. Neither boundedness of $\mathcal T$ nor a pre-existing t-structure on $\mathcal T$ is assumed.

proof.text: The subcategory $\mathcal B$ is strictly full: if $M\cong N$ in $\mathcal A$, functoriality gives $S(M)\cong S(N)$, so membership is preserved by strict fullness of $\mathcal T$. The complex $S(0)$ is the zero complex. Since $\mathcal T$ contains the ambient zero object, $0\in\mathcal B$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), degree-zero subcategory; zero and isomorphism closure

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], the single functor S is fully faithful. Both subcategories are full, so its restriction S:B→T is fully faithful. A single object has vanishing cohomology in all nonzero degrees; this transfers across isomorphisms. Conversely, for K in T with this vanishing, the ambient derived-category criteria isGE_iff and isLE_iff give K.IsGE 0 and K.IsLE 0. Apply [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] to obtain an object M and an isomorphism K≅S(M). Strict fullness transfers membership from K to S(M), so M belongs to B. This proves exactly the asserted essential-image characterization without requiring a t-structure on T.

source.place: Paragraph (2), identification of the degree-zero objects; Stacks Tags 06XS and 08J5

proof.text: Fix $f:M\to N$ in $\mathcal B$ and any distinguished cone triangle $S(M)\to S(N)\to D\to S(M)[1]$. Rotate it once by (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] to $S(N)\to D\to S(M)[1]\to S(N)[1]$. Its outer objects belong to $\mathcal T$ by shift closure. The extension closure in [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] and strict fullness therefore give $D\in\mathcal T$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), the cone belongs to the triangulated subcategory; Stacks Tag 05QM

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to this triangle. The single-complex cohomology calculation reduces the relevant part to $0\to H^{-1}(D)\to M\xrightarrow{f}N\to H^0(D)\to0$. Thus $H^{-1}(D)\to M$ is a kernel of $f$ and $N\to H^0(D)$ is a cokernel: exactness identifies the first monomorphism with $\ker f$ and the last epimorphism with $\operatorname{coker}f$. Their universal properties give the canonical isomorphisms claimed, relative to the chosen triangle. Since $D\in\mathcal T$, the hypothesis puts $S(H^{-1}(D))$ and $S(H^0(D))$ in $\mathcal T$. Strict fullness transfers this membership to every ambient kernel and cokernel of $f$, proving that they belong to $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Paragraph (2), kernel and cokernel calculation; Stacks Tags 05RS and 05RT

proof.text: Given any ambient short exact sequence $0\to M\to L\to N\to0$ with $M,N\in\mathcal B$, placing it in degree zero gives a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes (the other degrees are zero). By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] this yields a distinguished triangle $S(M)\to S(L)\to S(N)\to S(M)[1]$. Both outer objects lie in $\mathcal T$, so its extension closure and strict fullness give $S(L)\in\mathcal T$. Hence $L\in\mathcal B$.

For $M,N\in\mathcal B$, use the ambient biproduct in the abelian category $\mathcal A$. The sequence $0\to M\xrightarrow{\iota_M}M\oplus N\xrightarrow{\pi_N}N\to0$ is short exact: $\pi_M\iota_M=1$, $\pi_N\iota_N=1$, and $\iota_M\pi_M+\iota_N\pi_N=1$ show that $\iota_M$ is the kernel of $\pi_N$ and that $\pi_N$ is its cokernel. Step 5 gives $M\oplus N\in\mathcal B$. Together with step 1 and induction, this gives all finite ambient biproducts. Their universal properties restrict to the full subcategory.

source.place: Paragraph (2), the finite biproducts needed for the abelian-subcategory criterion

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-full-subcategory-exact] to $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal A$. Step 1 supplies an ambient zero object, step 4 supplies every ambient kernel and cokernel of a morphism between its objects, and step 6 supplies every ambient binary product (a biproduct), with all choices included by strict fullness. The lemma gives an abelian category with the inherited addition and ambient kernels and cokernels. Extension closure was proved in step 5. Only ambient derived-category facts and the stated cohomology closure were used; no boundedness or t-structure on $\mathcal T$ is required.
